Kavak Card for Draiver Operators - 2026/09/29 12:30 CST - Notes by Gemini
Invited: Kevin Burke, Fede Ranero, Armando Flores, dario.mattio@kavak.com, Paulo Ferrato, federico.boero@kavak.com

Summary
Financial providers reviewed and Mexican operational challenges addressed via parallel testing approved.
Regional Revenue And Providers: US accounts for 90 percent of revenue while international operations face tax deduction losses. Current financial partners include Ramp, PEX, Airbase, and Car IQ.
Mexican Operational Challenges: Mexico operations represent half of marketplace volume with significant tax losses from non-deductible foreign cards. Evaluation of Mendel and in-house Kavak cards provides potential solutions.
Technical Architecture And Testing: Contract with Mendel approved at zero cost for parallel testing alongside the Kavak card integration. Technical teams aligned on API evaluations and merchant category code controls.

Decisions (Aligned)
- Adoption of Kavak Card Solution: move forward with the in-house Kavak card rather than Mendel for driver expenses.
- Scheduling Technical Integration Meeting: Darío Mattio will schedule a technical meeting with Kevin Burke's team to review documentation and APIs.

Next steps
- [Kevin Burke] Review API Specifications: Review Pomelo integration documentation and Mendel API specs for compatibility with the Kavak card system.
- [Federico Boero, Darío Mattio] Provide CLI Access: Grant access to the Kavak CLI.
- [Armando Flores] Test Mendel Cards: Execute a pilot using Mendel cards for corporate travel expenses and a limited group of drivers. Monitor performance to validate tax deductibility and integration.
- [Federico Boero] Schedule Technical Call: Follow-up technical meeting to build the card operational solution for drivers.
- [Darío Mattio] Coordinate Technical Call: Discuss use case requirements with internal tech team and arrange meeting with external parties.
- [Kevin Burke] Review API Documentation: Compare provided documentation with the existing PEX implementation using AI; flag technical items.

Details
Mexico: PEX cards not accepted in ~50% of terminals; foreign-card expenses not tax deductible (loss of ~$5,000-$20,000/month in deductions); drivers get daily cash transfers when PEX fails. Mendel offers local virtual cards, API controls, AI receipt scanning for invoices. Kavak card: >85% approval rate in employee testing, virtual/physical, Google/Apple Pay, CLI for card creation, limits, on/off. Mendel and Kavak both run on Pomelo processor. Paulo: Mendel contract approved at zero commitment; Mexico is half of marketplace moves and a major finance bottleneck requiring fast resolution. Fede: priority is drivers; test should reflect fuel/tolls. Kevin prefers in-house Kavak integration (only create card, authorize, close calls).
